message.content:
The title of “best” jazz singer is highly subjective and depends on personal taste, vocal style, and the era you’re interested in. Below are some of the most celebrated jazz vocalists across different periods, each known for their unique contributions to the genre:

| Era | Singer | Notable Contributions |
|-----|--------|-----------------------|
| 1930s‑1940s | **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered a deeply emotive, improvisational style; iconic recordings like “Strange Fruit” and “God Bless the Child.” |
| 1940s‑1950s | **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” she mastered scat singing and delivered flawless diction on standards such as “Summertime.” |
| 1950s‑1960s | **Sarah Vaughan** | Renowned for her rich, operatic voice and wide vocal range; classics include “Misty” and “Lullaby of Birdland.” |
| 1960s‑1970s | **Tony Bennett** | Blended jazz with pop standards, delivering timeless performances of “I’ve Got You Under My Skin.” |
| 1970s‑1980s | **Cassandra Wilson** | Modern jazz vocalist who blends blues, folk, and world music; known for “The River” and “The Last Time I Saw Paris.” |
| 1990s‑2000s | **Norah Jones** | While more pop/folk, her jazz roots shine in “Come Away With Me.” |
| 2000s‑present | **Esperanza Spalding** | Multi‑instrumentalist and vocalist, blending jazz with funk and soul; known for “I Know You Know.” |

These artists represent a broad spectrum of jazz vocal styles—from the classic crooners of the early 20th century to contemporary innovators. If you’re looking for a specific style or era, let me know, and I can narrow down the list further!
